entities.name: PMID:25074740
observations: In 71 patients approximately 1 year after pulmonary embolism, those with ≥10% residual scintigraphic perfusion defects had longer clot-lysis time and higher PAI-1 than those with <10% defects; lysis time was independently associated with larger defects.
Residual defects occurred without echocardiographic or radiologic pulmonary hypertension, supporting an association outside established CTEPH.

entities.name: PMID:37932588
observations: In a prospective cohort of 79 acute PE patients, RPVO occurred in 23/79 (29.1%) at 3–6 months; RPVO was associated with lower fibrin-clot permeability and longer clot-lysis time at baseline and day 5–7.
Baseline clot permeability, D-dimer, and later E-selectin were independently associated with RPVO; the study supports a hypofibrinolytic/prothrombotic clot phenotype but does not establish causality.

entities.name: PMID:40544392
observations: In a small PADIS-PE ancillary analysis of 23 patients with first unprovoked PE, quantitative D-dimer, tPA, uPA, TFPI, and tissue-factor-based clot-lysis parameters were not associated with residual pulmonary vascular obstruction; 6/23 had RPVO.
The negative result conflicts with other cohorts but is limited by the small sample and selected population.

entities.name: PMID:36856592
observations: In a cross-sectional study of 46 CTEPH patients and 106 controls, fibrinogen Aα THR312ALA polymorphism was associated with CTEPH, with one genotype comparison showing OR 5.026 (95% CI 1.774–14.242).
This is indirect evidence compatible with altered fibrin structure or thrombophilia, not a direct functional fibrinolysis assay after acute PE.

entities.name: Residual PE hypofibrinolysis
observations: Across small human cohorts, residual perfusion defects or RPVO after PE are associated in several studies with prolonged clot-lysis time, elevated PAI-1, or dense less-permeable fibrin clots.
Evidence is heterogeneous and partly conflicting; available studies support association but do not establish that impaired fibrinolysis causes persistent obstruction.
